Future Present Labs
Protocol

One bus for every surface.

Unibus is a message transport protocol for display, audio, presence, sensors and control across heterogeneous machines.

Applications own their data and domain contracts. Unibus supplies envelopes, framing, routing and access grants.

A narrow transport contract

Envelopes
Messages carry routing information and bounded lifetime. The transport does not interpret application payloads.
Framing
A big-endian length prefix, JSON envelope and binary payload form the wire format.
Delivery
Commands, streams and snapshots have separate scheduling classes.
Connections
Router implementations support TCP and explicitly configured QUIC/TLS connections.

Grant-bearing connections

Node grants scope zones, namespaced capabilities, screen anchors, sites and roles. Authentication terminates at registration; application-level permissions remain with the owning service.

Network reachability alone is not permission to view a surface or control an instrument. Deployments must configure trust and grants.

Routers and adapters

The Rust workspace provides the protocol library, hub/router and adapters for services including MIDI, MQTT and ADB. Applications can advertise MCP tools and DCP decisions through provider-owned capability registries.
